unreg:score_path_functionals.reviewer: independent-NFL (Claude agent, agent verification, not human expert)
unreg:score_path_functionals.rederivation_notes: Own chain, written after reading only the contract wording (LEADCHANGE: at least 8 lead changes, first score excluded, trailing-or-tied team scores to lead; COMEBACK: winner trailed by 24+ at any point; LARGELEAD: band 7 to 10). Mechanism: pregame margin mean and volatility (team strength gap, total, QB/weather) -> number of possessions per team (pace, script) -> per-drive score outcome with point packages (TD 6+1/2, FG 3, safety 2, defensive scores) -> time-ordered score list -> running functionals (max |margin|, count of lead-taking scores after the first, winner's minimum margin) -> score-state feedback (trailers gamble, leaders kneel/run, QB benched) -> end of regulation and overtime treatment, which the text does not state. Required inputs: market-free offence/defence ratings, full-game drive-level outcome rates, QB status incl. in-game exit, fourth-down/2pt policy, pace/tempo, weather, tie/OT rules, rules text. Differences from the record: it covers all of this well and flags OT/band inclusivity as unresolved; but it leaves m.rules_text unattached, keeps spread-derived garbage_time/script, and omits in-game QB exit and any OT process input.

findings.text: Stage s5 and category_coverage.settlement_contract (COVERED) and required_data feeds_inputs cite m.rules_text, but the catalog entry unreg score_path_functionals carries 15 inputs and none is m.rules_text; the stage input id does not belong to the archetype inputs, so the settlement coverage claim rests on an input the archetype does not hold. Attach it to the catalog entry or change the coverage to GAP/NOT_ATTACHED.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: m.rules_text is now attached to the catalog entry (role primary) so stage s5 and settlement coverage rest on an input the archetype carries; detached-reference check returns 0.

findings.text: The record presents the path model as market-free, yet kept inputs nfl.garbage_time (measurement: probability of a 14+ lead in Q4 'from spread/total') and nfl.script (game states 'implied by spread/total', Gaussian margin around spread) are built from betting lines; input_audit marks them KEEP_SECONDARY/KEEP_CONTEXT without flagging this. Market-derived values enter s3 and s4 as inputs; re-measure from nfl.own_team_rating_market_free / model_team_points_mean or relabel as BENCHMARK_ONLY.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: nfl.garbage_time set BENCHMARK_ONLY, nfl.script and nfl.two_minute_tempo re-based on own-model margin distributions, new market-free input nfl.market_free_score_state_blowout_mass attached and staged; verified in merged catalog.

findings.text: nfl.drive_outcome_by_index is described as drives 1-3 and measured on the first four drives, yet opponent_matchup coverage and s2 use it as the opponent-adjusted per-drive generator for 10-12 drives; mid- and late-game drive rates exist only inside the nfl.score_path_sequence_sim measurement text, not as a standalone attached input.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: nfl.drive_result_lattice and nfl.period_drive_scoring_rates attached for mid and late drives; input_audit now scopes drive_outcome_by_index to the opening drives only.

findings.text: availability_news note says in-game QB exit is handled through nfl.garbage_time; that input's measurement covers blowout starter rest only, not injury exits, and nfl.in_game_exit_risk is not attached. A QB leaving changes comeback and lead-change odds; undisclosed as a gap.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: nfl.qb_blowout_pull_hazard and nfl.in_game_exit_risk attached and staged in s4; availability_news coverage cites them for mid-game quarterback exits.

findings.text: Stage s5 requires carrying both regulation-only and full-game readings, but no input models the overtime scoring process or overtime rules for regular-season games; only the contract ambiguity (u1) is disclosed, not the missing input.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: nfl.ot_total_increment and nfl.ot_ending_hazard attached and staged in s5; both regulation-only and full-game readings are carried, with the overtime ambiguity left in u1.

findings.text: Literal reading ('trailing or tied, scores to take a lead') counts a team retaking the lead from a tie (record's 7-0, 7-7, 14-7 example yields one lead change). Whether Kalshi counts this as a lead change is not flagged as ambiguous; it changes lead-change counts.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: new unresolved entry u4 (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS) states that a lead retaken from a tie is unverified as a lead change, and variants_and_edge_cases repeats it.

findings.text: Stale text from the former mixed record: input_audit reason for nfl.garbage_time says it 'was attached to the mixed archetype ... and is detached from the counting specials'. rules_verification is VERIFIED_FROM_RULES_TEXT although the text itself states no overtime, tie, postponement or source clause (PARTIALLY_VERIFIED fits better).
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: the stale 'mixed archetype' wording is gone from input_audit and rules_verification is now PARTIALLY_VERIFIED, matching a text with no overtime, tie, postponement or source clause.

findings.text: Statements calling the Feb 8, 2026 sample a 'championship game', the stakes effect on aggression, regulation-level rate 6-7 percent and 24-point comeback rate under one percent are not in the sampled text; the numerics are marked 'to recompute' but the championship/stakes framing is an outside inference. External sources (nflverse, Kalshi, PFR) could not be reached from this container (proxy 403), so nflverse field claims are unchecked.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: championship-game framing removed from u1 and other text; stakes effect labelled an unverified hypothesis (u3), numerics marked placeholders, provenance unverified flags kept; verified in merged record.

unreg:rare_play_call_events.reviewer: independent-NFL (Claude agent, agent verification, not human expert)
unreg:rare_play_call_events.rederivation_notes: Own chain, from the contract wording only (1YDPASS: team records at least one official forward pass attempt with line of scrimmage on or inside the opponent's 1 at the snap, sacks/scrambles/runs excluded, penalty-nullified attempts count if recorded; NONQBPASS: any non-QB pass attempt by either team, undefined). Mechanism for 1YD: snaps from the 1 (goal-to-go drive progress, short fields, penalties moving the ball to the 1, fourth-and-goal go decisions, and end-of-half clock situations such as a spike) -> pass vs sneak/run share at the 1 (coach/coordinator, personnel, QB mobility, down, opponent goal-line package) -> official-statistic definition. Non-QB: planned trick plays/fake kicks (coach hazard) plus emergency throws after QB exit, mapped to the official passer position. Required inputs: coach/play-caller, goal-line pass share by snap at the 1, trip volume, QB status/exit and QB depth chart, play-by-play with sack and nullified-play flags, rules text. Differences from the record: good coverage of coach and snap supply; it omits spikes and attaches rules text only in stages.

findings.text: Stages s5 and category_coverage (settlement_contract, officiating_rules) and required_data cite m.rules_text, but the catalog entry unreg rare_play_call_events carries 14 inputs and none is m.rules_text; stage input id does not belong to the archetype inputs.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: m.rules_text attached to the catalog entry as a primary input; stages s5/s6 and settlement and officiating coverage now cite an input the archetype holds (detached check 0).

findings.text: Missing mechanism: a quarterback spike (clock-stopping) on or inside the 1 near the end of a half is typically recorded as an incomplete pass attempt in play-by-play, so it could settle KXNFL1YDPASS (text excludes sacks, scrambles, runs, not spikes) and it is not a coach pass-call choice. No stage, input or unresolved entry addresses spikes or end-of-half goal-line clock management (nfl.two_minute_tempo is not attached). Add the stage, an input, and a CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS entry; whether Kalshi counts a spike is unverified.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: new input nfl.end_of_half_goal_line_snap_and_spike_probability defines end-of-half snaps from the 1 and P(spike), staged in s5, with CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS u4 on whether Kalshi counts a spike; market-free, NOT_COMPUTED.

findings.text: Non-QB emergency regime relies on generic nfl.in_game_exit_risk (position-agnostic probability of missing >25 percent of snaps); there is no QB-specific exit or QB2/emergency-passer depth input, so the emergency hazard in s3 is not actually measured by an attached input.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: nfl.qb_blowout_pull_hazard and nfl.weekly_qb_depth_slot_model attached for the quarterback-specific exit hazard; the missing emergency-passer identity is declared as u5.

findings.text: Internal inconsistency: s3 states per team-game P(at least one non-QB attempt) about 0.10-0.20, while the catalog measurement calls about 0.15 the league rate per game and later sums both teams; the magnitude is unverified and possibly too high. Also the goal_to_go_pass_rate nonlinearity wording ('rises from the 1 to the 5 ... falls again only inside the 2') is self-contradictory.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: s3 and the input measurement now both use the 0.15 per team-game unverified placeholder (both teams about 0.28); the goal_to_go_pass_rate nonlinearity wording is rewritten consistently.

findings.text: Unsupported assertions: catalog rationale says a Tush-Push team 'never passes from the 1'; heavy-right-tail coach concentration and environment NOT_APPLICABLE ('weather changes passing volume only slightly') are stated as fact without a source. rules_verification VERIFIED_FROM_RULES_TEXT although NONQBPASS has empty secondary text and no definition (PARTIALLY_VERIFIED fits better).
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: the Tush-Push assertion is removed, coach concentration is labelled an assumption, environment became GAP (u7) and rules_verification is PARTIALLY_VERIFIED.

findings.text: Catalog measurement counts 'pass_attempt == 1 (sacks and scrambles excluded)'; I believe nflverse pass_attempt flags include sacks, so sack == 0 and handling of no_play (penalty-nullified) rows would have to be applied explicitly, but I could not fetch the nflverse dictionary (proxy 403). Also unverified: FTN charting from 2022 only, passer position availability in nflverse, and the 'championship game' framing of the sample.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: pass_attempt semantics, no_play handling and spike flag declared SOURCE_UNVERIFIED in u6; measurement excludes sacks explicitly; championship claim removed from u2; verified in merged record.
